1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Add procedural cell mutation/evolution to the existing GENESIS game as a playable update grounded in real-world research.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” as the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected genome, cell-plate, evolution-view, and UI integration points.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes before edits.

### Active
- Implement procedural mutation/evolution and connect it to game UI and mechanics.
- Test the game and, if possible, capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement playable mutation/evolution using `generationStep()`, `advancePlateCells()`, `dividePlateCell()`, and `evolutionView()` in `app.js`.
2. Connect player actions and UI rendering to mutation/evolution mechanics.
3. Run checks and capture/inspect the latest screenshot if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Genome mutation, cell division, evolution view, simulation, and UI code.
- `index.html`: App shell and navigation.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styles.

## Important Context
- Existing mechanics include generation-level sequence mutations in `generationStep()` and cell-plate division/evolution in `advancePlateCells()` and `dividePlateCell()`.
- The “Advance 10 generations” button is rendered in `evolutionView()`; mutations currently occur per gene with a low model-defined rate, and the genome is replaced each generation.
- No changes are uncommitted; repository was clean at last check.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation/evolution to GENESIS, grounded in real-world research and integrated with its existing genome and cell systems.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” as the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected genome creation, cell division, simulation, and evolution UI in `app.js`; confirmed `node --check app.js` passes before implementation.
- Confirmed `dividePlateCell()` currently copies cells without mutation; `generationStep()` mutates the main genome; viruses are excluded from cell division.

### Active
- Add heritable, deterministic genome mutation on plate-cell division while preserving lineage and genome source data.
- Connect player controls to generation advancement and make evolutionary outcomes observable in the UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add mutation during cell division and retain parent/child lineage and genome records.
2. Connect player controls to evolution advancement and expose outcomes in the UI.
3. Run checks and, if possible, capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Genome mutation, cell division, evolution view, simulation, and UI code.
- `index.html`: App shell and navigation.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styles.

## Important Context
- `generationStep()` mutates the main genome; plate cells reference genomes through `S.plateSources` and `genomeId`.
- The Evolution view already has an “Advance 10 generations” button; the division mutation and UI action wiring remain to be implemented.

## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation/evolution to GENESIS, integrated with its existing genome and cell systems and grounded in real-world research.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” as the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected genome creation, cell division, simulation, and evolution UI in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `dividePlateCell()` copies cells without mutation; `generationStep()` mutates the main genome; viruses are excluded from cell division.
- Identified relevant functions and UI: `plateGenome()`, `cellView()`, existing “Advance 10 generations” control, and `data-action="evolve"`.

### Active
- Add heritable, deterministic genome mutation on plate-cell division while preserving lineage and genome source data.
- Connect player controls to generation advancement and make evolutionary outcomes observable in the UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement mutation during cell division and retain parent/child lineage and genome records.
2. Wire evolution controls and expose outcomes in the UI.
3. Run checks and, if possible, capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Genome mutation, cell division, evolution view, simulation, and UI code.
- `index.html`: App shell and navigation.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styles.

## Important Context
- `generationStep()` mutates the main genome; plate cells reference genomes through `S.plateSources` and `genomeId`.
- `dividePlateCell()` is currently a one-line function that creates a child with a deterministic division RNG but retains its parent’s `genomeId`.
- The Evolution view already has an “Advance 10 generations” button; division mutation and UI action wiring remain unimplemented.
- `node --check app.js` passed before implementation; no changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation/evolution to GENESIS, integrated with its genome and cell systems and grounded in real-world research.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” as the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected genome creation, cell division, simulation, and evolution UI in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `dividePlateCell()` copies cells without mutation; `generationStep()` mutates the main genome; viruses are excluded from cell division.
- Confirmed the Evolution view has an “Advance 10 generations” button and `cellView()` already provides cell/genome inspection UI.

### Active
- Add heritable, deterministic genome mutation on plate-cell division while preserving lineage and genome source data.
- Wire evolution controls and expose outcomes in the UI.
- Run checks and, if possible, capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement mutation during cell division and retain parent/child lineage and genome records.
2. Wire evolution controls and expose outcomes in the UI.
3. Run checks and, if possible, capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Genome mutation, cell division, evolution view, simulation, and UI code.
- `index.html`: App shell and navigation.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styles.

## Important Context
- No changes have been made yet; `node --check app.js` passed before implementation.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells refer to genomes through `genomeId`.
- `dividePlateCell()` currently retains the parent’s `genomeId`; it derives deterministic division RNG from seed, cell ID, and division count.
- Recent inspection confirmed `#view-root` is the render mount in `index.html`; no render/event-handler implementation was found in the inspected `app.js` contents.

## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation/evolution to GENESIS, integrated with its genome and cell systems and grounded in real-world research.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” as the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected genome creation, cell division, simulation, and evolution UI in `app.js`.
- Confirmed recent repository history does not contain the missing render/event-handler implementation.
- No code changes have been made; `git status --short` was clean during inspection.

### Active
- Investigate and restore or implement app rendering and event handling.
- Add heritable, deterministic genome mutation on plate-cell division while preserving lineage and genome source data.
- Wire evolution controls, expose mutation outcomes, run checks, and attempt the requested screenshot inspection.

### Blocked
- `app.js` ends at `genomeView()` with no render or event-handler implementation, so the app’s intended UI wiring must be restored or rebuilt before UI controls can be relied on.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `app.js` code and historical versions to understand existing views and state shape.
2. Implement rendering/event handling and deterministic mutation during cell division, retaining parent/child lineage and genome records.
3. Wire evolution controls, expose outcomes, run checks, and capture/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Genome, plate-cell division, simulation, evolution view, and partial UI code.
- `index.html`: App shell, navigation, and `#view-root` render mount.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styles.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells refer to genomes through `genomeId`.
- `dividePlateCell()` currently retains the parent’s `genomeId`; it derives deterministic division RNG from seed, cell ID, and division count.
- `generationStep()` mutates the main genome; viruses are excluded from cell division.
- Evolution view has an “Advance 10 generations” button, but no matching handler was found.
- `cellView()` provides cell/genome inspection UI; `#view-root` is the render mount in `index.html`.
- `overview()` includes `data-action="sample"` and `data-action="toggle"` controls; the app contains view markup but render and event-handler wiring remain absent.

## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation/evolution to GENESIS, integrated with its genome and cell systems and grounded in real-world research.
- Restore the missing app rendering/event wiring so the existing UI and controls function.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot with viewport width ≤1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” as the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.
- Preserve deterministic simulation behavior and genome lineage/source records during mutation and division.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected genome creation, plate-cell division, simulation, evolution UI, and app shell.
- Confirmed `app.js` currently ends at `genomeView()` with no render or event-handler wiring.
- Confirmed `dividePlateCell()` currently retains the parent `genomeId` and does not create heritable child-genome mutations.
- Confirmed `generationStep()` mutates the main genome and excludes viruses from cell division.
- Confirmed no code changes have been made; working tree was clean at last check.
- Compared historical `app.js` versions; older commits also contain view code but no restored final render/event-handler section.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering and event handling for existing views and controls.
- Add deterministic, heritable genome mutation during plate-cell division while preserving parent/child lineage and `S.plateSources`.
- Wire evolution controls, expose mutation outcomes, run checks, and capture/inspect the latest requested screenshot.

### Blocked
- UI controls cannot be reliably tested until render and event-handler wiring is implemented.
- No dedicated implementations were found for several sidebar destinations (`lab`, `notebook`, `archive`, `codex`), so routing may require identifying existing markup in truncated/omitted portions or adding suitable fallback views.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete tail of `app.js` and historical versions to recover any missing render/event-handler implementation.
2. Implement `render()` and delegated event handling for navigation, simulation controls, genome/cell interactions, archive actions, and evolution.
3. Modify `dividePlateCell()` to derive a deterministic child genome from the parent genome, record mutation metadata, assign a new `genomeId`, and store the child source in `S.plateSources`.
4. Ensure lineage and mutation outcomes are visible in cell/genome/evolution views without mutating parent genome records.
5. Run syntax/runtime checks and use the provided capture workflow to create and inspect only the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Genome generation, plate-cell simulation/division, views, and missing render/event wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, top-bar controls, `#view-root`, toast/modal mounts.
- `style.css`: Existing layout and UI styling, including cell-plate and research views.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entrypoint.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing prior screenshot; replace/use only a newly captured latest screenshot for inspection.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference genomes through `genomeId`.
- `dividePlateCell()` is at `app.js:73`; `generationStep()` is at `app.js:76`; `render`/event handlers are absent after `genomeView()` at line 97.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells with a shared genome ID and source snapshot; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome from `S.plateSources`.
- Existing controls include `data-action="sample"`, `toggle`, `evolve`, `sequence`, `save-genome`, `clear-inspection`, `load-plate-preset`, `plate-archive`; navigation uses `data-view`; speed controls use `data-speed`; plate cells use `data-plate-cell`; genes use `data-gene`.
- `evolutionView()` provides “Advance 10 generations” via `data-action="evolve"` but currently has no handler.
- `index.html` navigation targets `overview`, `genome`, `cell`, `evolution`, `lab`, `notebook`, `archive`, and `codex`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation/evolution to GENESIS, integrated with genome and cell systems while preserving existing UI rendering and controls.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Preserve deterministic simulation behavior and genome lineage/source records during mutation and division.
- Exclude viruses from cell division.
- Save and inspect only the latest small JPEG screenshot with viewport width ≤1280px.

## Decisions
- Use the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems; interpret “New form” within those systems.
- Heritable plate divisions create new child genome IDs while retaining parent genomes and lineage/source records.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Child genomes clone parents and receive 1–2 deterministic coding mutations with cumulative mutation metadata.
- Modify the effective later `cellView()`, `genomeView()`, and `evolutionView()` implementations rather than adding duplicates.
- Preserve existing fallback views and restored `app.js` implementation from commit `6405445`.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added plate-cell lineage and mutation defaults, including `parentGenomeId`, `lineageOrigin`, `generation`, `mutationCount`, and `mutationDetails`.
- Added persisted-state migration defaults for older cells.
- Added deterministic `mutatePlateGenome()` with cumulative mutation records and recalculated sequences.
- Updated `dividePlateCell()` to reject viruses, preserve parents, register child genomes in `S.plateSources`, assign daughter lineage metadata, and emit deterministic generation events.
- Added deterministic daughter positioning and inherited cell-state initialization.
- Updated `cellView()` with cell-cycle, checkpoint, lineage, genome, and mutation state.
- Added lineage/mutation summaries to `genomeView()` and `evolutionView()`.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Generated and inspected `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/genesis-latest.jpeg`; it is a 1200×900 JPEG.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

### Active
- Runtime validation of seeded plate division, repeated deterministic results, persisted migration, manual cell-cycle behavior, and virus non-division.
- The attempted Node VM validation failed because the evaluated prefix did not expose `S` as expected (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'plate')`); browser-level behavior still needs validation.

### Blocked
- No external blocker; deterministic runtime test needs to be corrected or exercised in a browser.

## Next Move
1. Run the app in a browser and select a viable plate cell.
2. Trigger `cell-cycle`; verify a daughter appears with a distinct genome ID, mutation details, source record, parent linkage, and generation metadata.
3. Repeat equivalent seeded setups and compare child IDs, mutations, positions, and source records for determinism.
4. Verify virus entities cannot divide.
5. Verify the new lineage/mutation summaries render in Genome explorer and Evolution.
6. Re-run syntax/diff checks and inspect the latest screenshot only.
7. Report assumptions, validation results, and that changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: simulation state, mutation/division logic, migration, views, persistence, and event handlers.
- `index.html`: navigation and delegated controls.
- `style.css`: dashboard, plate, genome, and evolution presentation.
- `capture.sh`: screenshot capture entrypoint.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: latest visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to source genome records; cells resolve genomes through `plateGenome(cell)`.
- `mutatePlateGenome()` clones with `makeGenome(seed,parent)`, applies deterministic coding mutations, preserves cumulative mutation metadata, and recalculates `child.sequence`.
- `dividePlateCell()` requires `cycleProgress >= 1`, a `PASS` checkpoint, non-virus status, and a plate size below 30.
- The parent retains its genome; daughters receive `sourceLabel: 'MUTATED DAUGHTER'`, `parentGenomeId`, `lineageOrigin`, generation, and inherited mutation details.
- The latest screenshot was copied to `genesis-latest.jpeg`; repository status shows modified `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`.

## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation and evolution to GENESIS, integrated with genome and cell systems while preserving existing UI rendering and controls.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Preserve deterministic simulation behavior and genome lineage/source records during mutation and division.
- Exclude viruses from cell division.
- Save and inspect only the latest small JPEG screenshot with viewport width ≤1280px.
- Report validation results, assumptions, and that changes remain uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” within the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.
- Heritable plate divisions create new child genome IDs while retaining parent genomes and lineage/source records.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Child genomes clone parents and receive 1–2 deterministic coding mutations with cumulative mutation metadata.
- Modify the effective later `cellView()`, `genomeView()`, and `evolutionView()` implementations rather than adding duplicates.
- Preserve existing fallback views and the restored `app.js` implementation from commit `6405445`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added plate-cell lineage and mutation defaults and migration defaults for older persisted cells.
- Added deterministic `mutatePlateGenome()` and updated `dividePlateCell()` with virus exclusion, parent preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events.
- Added deterministic daughter positioning and inherited cell-state initialization.
- Updated cell, genome, and evolution views with cycle/checkpoint, lineage, genome, and mutation details.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- A fixed-seed runtime harness verified division creates a daughter with distinct genome ID, mutation details, source record, parent linkage, generation, and position; equivalent seeded runs matched exactly.
- Runtime harness verified virus division is rejected without changing plate size.
- Latest screenshot artifact is `genesis-latest.jpeg`, a 1200×900 JPEG.
- Changes remain uncommitted: `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are modified.

### Active
- Finish runtime validation of persisted-state migration, manual cell-cycle behavior, and lineage/mutation summary rendering in Genome explorer and Evolution.

### Blocked
- The Node VM harness stops before later view declarations; invoking `handleAction('cell-cycle')` triggers `render()` and fails with `ReferenceError: genomeView is not defined`. Earlier cutoffs also failed because `plateGenome` was not yet defined. Direct division validation succeeds when evaluation includes `plateGenome()`.

## Next Move
1. Adjust the harness to include the view declarations while avoiding browser startup, or validate manual interaction in a browser.
2. Verify manual cell-cycle progression and lineage/mutation UI rendering.
3. Validate persisted-state migration for older cells.
4. Re-run `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, and inspect only the latest `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
5. Report assumptions, validation results, and uncommitted status.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: simulation state, mutation/division logic, migration, views, persistence, and event handlers.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: latest 1200×900 visual verification artifact.
- `index.html`: navigation and delegated controls.
- `style.css`: dashboard, plate, genome, and evolution presentation.
- `capture.sh`: screenshot capture entrypoint.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to source genome records; cells resolve genomes through `plateGenome(cell)`.
- `dividePlateCell()` requires `cycleProgress >= 1`, a `PASS` checkpoint, non-virus status, and a plate size below 30.
- A daughter’s source genome has `origin` set to the parent genome ID; its cell has `parentGenomeId`, `lineageOrigin`, generation, and cumulative mutation metadata.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e44600ea7ffeyihiqna1YD2z1V" state="completed">
## Recommendation

Add a **per-cell `cellTypeId`** that refers to a small, static cell-type registry. Keep it separate from `genomeId`: the genome describes inherited sequence and traits, while the cell type is an explicit classification assigned to an individual cell.

For GENESIS’s current model, the most coherent realistic default is a **unicellular green-algal cell**—the app already describes its organism as a unicellular phototroph and shows a Chlamydomonas-referenced schematic. Avoid offering unrelated types such as neurons or epithelial cells unless the simulation also establishes a multicellular organism context. Treat type as descriptive/visual metadata initially; don’t imply it changes simulated behavior unless that behavior is explicitly modeled.

## Minimal assignment behavior

- Give every newly initialized cell the same default type.
- Add a native type selector to the **selected-cell detail area** so the user can classify individual cells.
- Have newly added cells inherit the currently selected cell’s type; daughter cells already copy their parent’s fields in `dividePlateCell(...)`, so the type will naturally be inherited there.
- When loading older saved state, fill in a valid default for cells that have no type field—or have an unrecognized type ID. `storeState()` serializes the state to local storage, so the new field will persist automatically.

A small registry keyed by stable IDs is preferable to storing display names on each cell. It could hold a label and concise description; add visual metadata only if the plate rendering needs it. Keep the list deliberately narrow until the biological scope of the simulation is broader.

## Where it fits

- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js ):  
  - `makePlateState(...)` creates the initial cells; assign the default type there.
  - The state-normalization loop after `loadState()` is the backward-compatible place to validate or default `cellTypeId`.
  - `cellView()` already builds the selected-cell details and is the smallest place for a selector.
  - `plateCellMarkup(cell)` renders each plate cell; it can display a small type cue if that’s useful, but the per-cell detail selector is enough for a minimal version.
  - `addCellsToPlate(...)` should set the type explicitly for newly added cells, following the inheritance policy above.
  - `dividePlateCell(...)` creates daughters with `{...cell,...}`; parent type will carry over unless deliberately overridden.
  - The document-level delegated click handler selects plate cells. A `<select>` will need a `change` handler that updates the selected cell’s `cellTypeId`, persists state, and re-renders.

- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css ):  
  Existing `.plate-stage`, `.plate-cell`, and detail-card styling can accommodate a compact selector or label. If types receive colors or badges, make them supplemental to the existing selected/stressed/stained indicators and preserve readable contrast.

- [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html ):  
  No shell or navigation change appears necessary; the observatory is already a navigation view.

## Important distinction

Do not use `genome.species` as the cell type. `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a genome by `genomeId`, and archived genomes can have species labels, but those describe genome/source records—not a per-cell classification. Keeping `cellTypeId` independent avoids conflating cell identity with genome lineage.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add playable procedural cell mutation and evolution to GENESIS, integrated with genome and cell systems while preserving existing UI rendering and controls.

## Requirements
- Implement without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Preserve deterministic simulation behavior and genome lineage/source records during mutation and division.
- Exclude viruses from cell division.
- Save and inspect only the latest small JPEG screenshot with viewport width ≤1280px.
- Report validation results, assumptions, and that changes remain uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Interpret “New form” within the existing GENESIS cell and evolution systems.
- Heritable plate divisions create new child genome IDs while retaining parent genomes and lineage/source records.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Child genomes clone parents and receive 1–2 deterministic coding mutations with cumulative mutation metadata.
- Modify the effective later `cellView()`, `genomeView()`, and `evolutionView()` implementations rather than adding duplicates.
- Preserve existing fallback views and the restored `app.js` implementation from commit `6405445`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added plate-cell lineage and mutation defaults and migration defaults for older persisted cells.
- Added deterministic `mutatePlateGenome()` and updated `dividePlateCell()` with virus exclusion, parent preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events.
- Added deterministic daughter positioning and inherited cell-state initialization.
- Updated cell, genome, and evolution views with cycle/checkpoint, lineage, genome, and mutation details.
- VM harness passed migration-default, manual division/lineage, genome lineage-rendering, and Evolution summary checks.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg`: 1200×900 JPEG, within the requested width limit.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: simulation state, migration, mutation/division logic, views, persistence, and event handlers.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: latest visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to source genome records; cells resolve genomes through `plateGenome(cell)`.
- `dividePlateCell()` requires `cycleProgress >= 1`, a `PASS` checkpoint, non-virus status, and a plate size below 30.
- A daughter’s source genome has `origin` set to the parent genome ID; its cell has `parentGenomeId`, `lineageOrigin`, generation, and cumulative mutation metadata.
- Changes remain uncommitted: `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg` are modified.

[ref. ID; 3490]
The cell is usually ovoid, has a single cup-shaped chloroplast with a pyrenoid and two contractile vacuoles at the bases of the flagella, and is surrounded with a thin cellulose wall and a thick gelatinous sheath. (ref. ID; 3490)

Chlamydomonas antarcticus Wille (ref. ID; 3491)

See; Chlamydomonas eugametos Moewus (ref. ID; 3718)
Chlamydomonas reginae Ettl & Green, 1973 (ref. ID; 3718)
Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (ref. ID; 3721, 4189)
Chlamydomonas simplex (Pascher) (ref. ID; 3490)


Chlamydomonas bullosa Butcher, 1959 (ref. ID; 3721)
Descriptions

Light microscopy: Cell length ranges from 10 um to 14.4 um (average 12 um). The average width of cells is 10 um. Young cells are narrowly ovoid, becoming more broadly ovoid as they age. The cell wall is prominent but distant from the periplast, and extends to a distinct saddle-shaped papilla. The chromatophore is apple green, cup-shaped and has a narrow but deep sinus. The nucleus is easily distinguishable, being located in an anterior position in the sinus of the chromatophore. The pyrenoid is round to oval and is in the posterior half of the cell. Some cells had two pyrenoids. The elongated eyespot is in an antero-median position. The two flagella are equal to the length of the cell. In cell division up to four daughter cells are produced. (ref. ID; 3721)
Electron microscopy: The cell is bounded by a cell wall 80 nm in thickness, composed of several layers. Immediately inside the cell wall is a pitted granular layer in close proximity to the bounding membrane of the chloroplast. The thickness of this layer varies from 30 to 160 nm, and the pits are typically 100 nm in diameter. The overall thickness of the cell surface structure is 330 nm. The granular layer is an extension of the cytoplasm into the space between the chloroplast and the outer cell wall. The nucleus is roughly spherical, and typically 2.4 um in diameter. The nucleolus has a smooth regular outline, and is 1.4 um in diameter. Mitochondria are numerous throughout the cell and may be spherical, ranging in diameter from 550 to 950 nm, or elongated, reaching up to 2.7 um in length. Golgi bodies are located throughout the cell 7 to 9 saccules were observed in the stacks, which measured from 240 to 370 nm across. The saccules are flatly stacked, and a maximum of 6 golgi bodies per cell were observed. At least two are closely associated with the nucleus. The pyrenoid is spherical, posterior to median in position, and is typically 3 um in diameter. It is surrounded by a starch sheath 4 um across, which is penetrated by numerous chloroplast thylakoids with bundles of 2-4 lamellae. The chloroplast occurs in all parts of the cell, between other cell components. The intraplastidial eyespot is up to 1 um long. It consists of a double layer of pigment granules. Rough endoplasmic reticulum occurs throughout the cell. (ref. ID; 3721)


Chlamydomonas simplex (Pascher) (ref. ID; 3490)
Descriptions
The simple spherical species, 17-20 um in diameter. (ref. ID; 3490)

			The Resource Center is funded by the National Science Foundation and located in the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology at the University of Minnesota. Our mission is to maintain and distribute materials for Chlamydomonas research and to provide information to researchers.
Chlamydomonas is a haploid unicellular eukaryote; each cell contains a chloroplast similar to those of plants and swims with two flagella (cilia) similar to those found in numerous other eukaryotic groups including mammals. In 2007, the haploid nuclear genome was sequenced and found to encode approximately 15,000 genes. The mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes also have been sequenced.
For more than 50 years, Chlamydomonas has served as a useful experimental system for genetics research on chloroplast biogenesis and function, flagellar assembly and motility, metabolic pathways (including lipid production), the circadian clock, and many other fundamental biological processes. Mutant strains generated in these studies are maintained and distributed by the Resource Center.
The Chlamy Center is supported by the National Science Foundation Living Stock Collections for Biological Research program (grant numbers 0951671 & 00017383) and by users like you.  Thank you for your support.

## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing procedural mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Keep cell type as descriptive per-cell metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Use a unicellular green-algal cell as the default context; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact cell-type registry grounded in real-world research, with the existing green-algal framing as the default.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events.
- Added lineage and mutation details to cell, genome, and evolution views; prior VM checks, `node --check app.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Identified relevant cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.
- Found research references: NIES Chlamydomonas morphology page (`https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm`) and Chlamydomonas Resource Center (`https://www.chlamycollection.org/`), which describes *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as a haploid unicellular green alga with a chloroplast and two flagella.

### Active
- Add selectable, research-based cell-type metadata to the observatory, including initialization, migration, inheritance, and UI controls.

### Blocked
- Web searches were cancelled; additional literature sources remain to be established if needed.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate existing cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to the selected-cell details; preserve type on daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: latest visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes plate cells; `addCellsToPlate()` creates added cells; `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division requires `cycleProgress >= 1`, a `PASS` checkpoint, non-virus status, and plate size below 30.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`; changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing procedural mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Keep cell type as descriptive per-cell metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Use a unicellular green-algal cell as the default context; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact cell-type registry grounded in real-world research, with the existing green-algal framing as the default.
- Use *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events.
- Added lineage and mutation details to cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Identified cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.
- Found research references: [Chlamydomonas Resource Center](https://www.chlamycollection.org/) and NIES morphology page (URL below).

### Active
- Add selectable cell-type metadata to the observatory, including initialization, migration, inheritance, and UI controls.

### Blocked
- Web searches were cancelled; additional literature sources have not been established.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate existing cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: latest visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes plate cells; `addCellsToPlate()` creates added cells; `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division requires `cycleProgress >= 1`, a `PASS` checkpoint, non-virus status, and plate size below 30; division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Research reference: https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm; the Chlamydomonas Resource Center describes *C. reinhardtii* as a research green-alga culture collection.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is per-cell descriptive metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature sources have not been established; prior web searches were cancelled.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest `git diff --check` passed.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division uses seeds of the form `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

The Resource Center is funded by the National Science Foundation and located in the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology at the University of Minnesota. Our mission is to maintain and distribute materials for Chlamydomonas research and to provide information to researchers.

Chlamydomonas is a haploid unicellular eukaryote; each cell contains a chloroplast similar to those of plants and swims with two flagella (cilia) similar to those found in numerous other eukaryotic groups including mammals. In 2007, the haploid nuclear genome was sequenced and found to encode approximately 15,000 genes. The mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes also have been sequenced.

For more than 50 years, Chlamydomonas has served as a useful experimental system for genetics research on chloroplast biogenesis and function, flagellar assembly and motility, metabolic pathways (including lipid production), the circadian clock, and many other fundamental biological processes. Mutant strains generated in these studies are maintained and distributed by the Resource Center.

The Chlamy Center is supported by the National Science Foundation Living Stock Collections for Biological Research program (grant numbers 0951671 & 00017383) and by users like you.  Thank you for your support.

# *Chlamydomonas*

***Chlamydomonas* Ehrenberg** (formerly Protozoa, now Green alga)

\[ref. ID; 3490\]  
The cell is usually ovoid, has a single cup-shaped chloroplast with a pyrenoid and two contractile vacuoles at the bases of the flagella, and is surrounded with a thin cellulose wall and a thick gelatinous sheath. (ref. ID; 3490)

1. ***Chlamydomonas antarcticus*** Wille (ref. ID; 3491)

2. ***[Chlamydomonas bullosa](#Chlamydomonas%20bullosa)*** Butcher, 1959 (ref. ID; 3721)

3. ***Chlamydomonas eugametos*** Moewus (ref. ID; 3718)  
Syn; ***Chlamydomonas moewusii*** Gerloff (ref. ID; 3718)

4. ***Chlamydomonas geitleri*** Ettl (ref. ID; 3709)

5. ***Chlamydomonas moewusii*** Gerloff  
See; ***Chlamydomonas eugametos*** Moewus (ref. ID; 3718)

6. ***Chlamydomonas reginae*** Ettl & Green, 1973 (ref. ID; 3718)

7. ***Chlamydomonas reinhardtii*** (ref. ID; 3721, 4189)

8. ***[Chlamydomonas simplex](#Chlamydomonas%20simplex)*** (Pascher) (ref. ID; 3490)

---

### *[Chlamydomonas bullosa]()* Butcher, 1959 (ref. ID; 3721)

#### Descriptions

- Light microscopy: Cell length ranges from 10 um to 14\.4 um (average 12 um). The average width of cells is 10 um. Young cells are narrowly ovoid, becoming more broadly ovoid as they age. The cell wall is prominent but distant from the periplast, and extends to a distinct saddle-shaped papilla. The chromatophore is apple green, cup-shaped and has a narrow but deep sinus. The nucleus is easily distinguishable, being located in an anterior position in the sinus of the chromatophore. The pyrenoid is round to oval and is in the posterior half of the cell. Some cells had two pyrenoids. The elongated eyespot is in an antero-median position. The two flagella are equal to the length of the cell. In cell division up to four daughter cells are produced. (ref. ID; 3721)

- Electron microscopy: The cell is bounded by a cell wall 80 nm in thickness, composed of several layers. Immediately inside the cell wall is a pitted granular layer in close proximity to the bounding membrane of the chloroplast. The thickness of this layer varies from 30 to 160 nm, and the pits are typically 100 nm in diameter. The overall thickness of the cell surface structure is 330 nm. The granular layer is an extension of the cytoplasm into the space between the chloroplast and the outer cell wall. The nucleus is roughly spherical, and typically 2\.4 um in diameter. The nucleolus has a smooth regular outline, and is 1\.4 um in diameter. Mitochondria are numerous throughout the cell and may be spherical, ranging in diameter from 550 to 950 nm, or elongated, reaching up to 2\.7 um in length. Golgi bodies are located throughout the cell 7 to 9 saccules were observed in the stacks, which measured from 240 to 370 nm across. The saccules are flatly stacked, and a maximum of 6 golgi bodies per cell were observed. At least two are closely associated with the nucleus. The pyrenoid is spherical, posterior to median in position, and is typically 3 um in diameter. It is surrounded by a starch sheath 4 um across, which is penetrated by numerous chloroplast thylakoids with bundles of 2-4 lamellae. The chloroplast occurs in all parts of the cell, between other cell components. The intraplastidial eyespot is up to 1 um long. It consists of a double layer of pigment granules. Rough endoplasmic reticulum occurs throughout the cell. (ref. ID; 3721)

---

### *[Chlamydomonas simplex]()* (Pascher) (ref. ID; 3490)

#### Descriptions

The simple spherical species, 17-20 um in diameter. (ref. ID; 3490)

## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is per-cell descriptive metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature sources have not been established; prior web searches were cancelled.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest `git diff --check` passed.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division uses seeds of the form `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is per-cell descriptive metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature sources have not been established; prior web searches were cancelled.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest `git diff --check` passed.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division uses seeds of the form `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

			The Resource Center is funded by the National Science Foundation and located in the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology at the University of Minnesota. Our mission is to maintain and distribute materials for Chlamydomonas research and to provide information to researchers.
Chlamydomonas is a haploid unicellular eukaryote; each cell contains a chloroplast similar to those of plants and swims with two flagella (cilia) similar to those found in numerous other eukaryotic groups including mammals. In 2007, the haploid nuclear genome was sequenced and found to encode approximately 15,000 genes. The mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes also have been sequenced.
For more than 50 years, Chlamydomonas has served as a useful experimental system for genetics research on chloroplast biogenesis and function, flagellar assembly and motility, metabolic pathways (including lipid production), the circadian clock, and many other fundamental biological processes. Mutant strains generated in these studies are maintained and distributed by the Resource Center.
The Chlamy Center is supported by the National Science Foundation Living Stock Collections for Biological Research program (grant numbers 0951671 & 00017383) and by users like you.  Thank you for your support.

[ref. ID; 3490]
The cell is usually ovoid, has a single cup-shaped chloroplast with a pyrenoid and two contractile vacuoles at the bases of the flagella, and is surrounded with a thin cellulose wall and a thick gelatinous sheath. (ref. ID; 3490)

Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (ref. ID; 3721, 4189)
Chlamydomonas simplex (Pascher) (ref. ID; 3490)


Chlamydomonas bullosa Butcher, 1959 (ref. ID; 3721)
Descriptions

Light microscopy: Cell length ranges from 10 um to 14.4 um (average 12 um). The average width of cells is 10 um. Young cells are narrowly ovoid, becoming more broadly ovoid as they age. The cell wall is prominent but distant from the periplast, and extends to a distinct saddle-shaped papilla. The chromatophore is apple green, cup-shaped and has a narrow but deep sinus. The nucleus is easily distinguishable, being located in an anterior position in the sinus of the chromatophore. The pyrenoid is round to oval and is in the posterior half of the cell. Some cells had two pyrenoids. The elongated eyespot is in an antero-median position. The two flagella are equal to the length of the cell. In cell division up to four daughter cells are produced. (ref. ID; 3721)
Electron microscopy: The cell is bounded by a cell wall 80 nm in thickness, composed of several layers. Immediately inside the cell wall is a pitted granular layer in close proximity to the bounding membrane of the chloroplast. The thickness of this layer varies from 30 to 160 nm, and the pits are typically 100 nm in diameter. The overall thickness of the cell surface structure is 330 nm. The granular layer is an extension of the cytoplasm into the space between the chloroplast and the outer cell wall. The nucleus is roughly spherical, and typically 2.4 um in diameter. The nucleolus has a smooth regular outline, and is 1.4 um in diameter. Mitochondria are numerous throughout the cell and may be spherical, ranging in diameter from 550 to 950 nm, or elongated, reaching up to 2.7 um in length. Golgi bodies are located throughout the cell 7 to 9 saccules were observed in the stacks, which measured from 240 to 370 nm across. The saccules are flatly stacked, and a maximum of 6 golgi bodies per cell were observed. At least two are closely associated with the nucleus. The pyrenoid is spherical, posterior to median in position, and is typically 3 um in diameter. It is surrounded by a starch sheath 4 um across, which is penetrated by numerous chloroplast thylakoids with bundles of 2-4 lamellae. The chloroplast occurs in all parts of the cell, between other cell components. The intraplastidial eyespot is up to 1 um long. It consists of a double layer of pigment granules. Rough endoplasmic reticulum occurs throughout the cell. (ref. ID; 3721)


Chlamydomonas simplex (Pascher) (ref. ID; 3490)
Descriptions
The simple spherical species, 17-20 um in diameter. (ref. ID; 3490)

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is per-cell descriptive metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature sources have not been established; prior web searches were cancelled.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest `git diff --check` passed.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is per-cell descriptive metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`.
- Confirmed initial research context via the Chlamydomonas Resource Center and a morphology reference describing *Chlamydomonas* as a green alga.
- Reviewed current cell initialization, migration, division, rendering, and event-handler code; `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were cancelled; available sources provide initial context.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest `git diff --check` passed.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is per-cell descriptive metadata, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`; reviewed their current behavior.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were previously cancelled; initial references provide context, but further research remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is descriptive metadata per cell, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Located cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code in `app.js`; reviewed current behavior.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were previously cancelled; initial references provide context, but further research remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is descriptive metadata per cell, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default biological context; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Reviewed cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were previously cancelled; initial references provide context, but further research remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest status showed both modified.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.
- Latest `git diff --check` passes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving its existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is descriptive metadata per cell, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default biological context; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Reviewed cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were previously cancelled; further research remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest status showed both modified, with `git diff --check` passing.
- `makePlateState()` initializes cells, `addCellsToPlate()` adds them, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells; cell clicks update `S.selectedCellId`.
- The current `cellView()` falls back to `Pelagomyces isolate`; organelle display includes Golgi and lysosomes, which may need to be reconciled with the unicellular algal framing.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm.

## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is descriptive metadata per cell, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default biological context; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Reviewed cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were previously cancelled; further research remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest status showed both modified, with `git diff --check` passing.
- Most recent inspection confirmed no cell-type registry or selector is implemented yet; `makePlateState()` and `addCellsToPlate()` create cells, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Current `cellView()` falls back to `Pelagomyces isolate`; organelle display includes Golgi and lysosomes, which may need reconciliation with the unicellular algal framing.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add realistic, research-based, selectable cell types to GENESIS while preserving existing mutation, evolution, lineage, UI, and control systems.

## Requirements
- Cell type is descriptive metadata per cell, separate from genome traits.
- Keep the unicellular green-algal framing as the default biological context; avoid unrelated multicellular cell types.
- New cells inherit the selected cell’s type; daughter cells inherit their parent’s type.
- Migrate older saved cells and preserve deterministic simulation behavior.

## Decisions
- Use a compact registry of realistic cell types, with *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* as the default biological context.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing deterministic plate-cell mutation and division, virus exclusion, parent-genome preservation, child genome/source registration, lineage metadata, and generation events are implemented.
- Lineage and mutation details are present in cell, genome, and evolution views.
- Reviewed cell initialization, migration, division, observatory rendering, and click-handler code.

### Active
- Implement the cell-type registry, initialization and migration, inheritance during division, and observatory selector/context UI.

### Blocked
- Additional literature searches were previously cancelled; further research remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Add a compact realistic cell-type registry and default algal assignment in `app.js`; migrate saved cells and assign types to newly added cells.
2. Add a selector and concise research context to selected-cell details; preserve type during daughter-cell division.
3. Validate determinism, migration, inheritance, and UI; refresh `genesis-latest.jpeg` if visual verification is available.
4. Report validation, assumptions, sources, and uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: cell state, migration, division, observatory rendering, and event handlers.
- `style.css`: observatory and selector styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: visual verification artifact.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; latest status showed both modified, with `git diff --check` passing.
- Most recent inspection confirmed no cell-type registry or selector is implemented yet; `makePlateState()` and `addCellsToPlate()` create cells, and `dividePlateCell()` spreads parent state into daughter cells.
- Current `cellView()` falls back to `Pelagomyces isolate`; organelle display includes Golgi and lysosomes, which may need reconciliation with the unicellular algal framing.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; `plateGenome(cell)` resolves a cell’s genome.
- Division seeds use `${S.seed}:${cell.id}:${cell.divisions}:division`.
- Research references: https://www.chlamycollection.org/ and https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/morpho/flagella/chla-nas.htm
